summary: Trinity speaks two lines of reassurance, stating that the person in question is going to make it. The scene contains no action description, only these two lines of dialogue.

what_changes.before: Uncertainty or concern about the outcome
what_changes.after: Assertion that the person will survive
what_changes.evidence: Don't worry. He's going to make it.

event_hint.one_line: Trinity reassures someone that Neo will survive the pursuit.

minds.wants: To stabilize the emotional state of the crew and maintain the operational focus on retrieving Neo before the sentinels arrive.
minds.feels: A desperate, controlled anxiety. She is aware of the high probability of failure given the 5-minute window, but she is forcing herself to project certainty to prevent panic from spreading to Tank or Morpheus.
minds.shows: Calm, authoritative reassurance. Her tone is flat and directive, stripping away the uncertainty of the previous moment.

believes_about.belief: Neo has the instinct or capability to survive the immediate threat of Agent Smith's pursuit.
believes_about.wrong_because: This belief is currently a hope rather than a fact; Neo is still in the Matrix and has not yet demonstrated his ability to stop bullets or outmaneuver Smith in a sustained chase.

minds.basis: In sc-213, Trinity asks 'How long?' and receives 'Five minutes. Maybe six.' In sc-214, she objects to the EMP usage because Neo is not out. The shift from her panic ('Oh no') in sc-213 to 'Don't worry' here indicates a conscious decision to manage the team's morale rather than report the raw data of their precarious position.

connects_back: sc-213: The establishment of the 5-minute countdown and the discovery of the sentinels.
sc-214: Morpheus's decision to hold the EMP, creating the time pressure that necessitates Trinity's reassurance.
sets_up: sc-216: Neo's frantic call to Tank and Trinity's subsequent command to 'get your ass back here,' which contrasts with the calm assurance given in this scene.
dramatic_function: This scene serves as a moment of false security. By asserting that Neo will make it, Trinity raises the stakes; if she is wrong, her confidence becomes a source of shame and frustration for the team, intensifying the tension before the inevitable failure of the first escape attempt.
